objective: To spell -ing forms that require doubling the final consonant
defs: resting with your weight on your bottom
moving through water using arms and legs
placing something in a particular spot
jumping lightly or leaving something out

sentences.forgetting: He kept ____________________ his locker number, so he had to ask the caretaker every single morning.
sentences.beginning: She was just ____________________ to understand why the magician refused to ever repeat a trick.
sentences.sitting: The heron was ____________________ perfectly still at the edge of the lake, waiting for a fish to pass.
sentences.running: The courier was ____________________ late and left parcels on every doorstep without knocking.
sentences.swimming: The club was ____________________ lengths in the outdoor pool every weekend, even in November.
sentences.shopping: They were ____________________ for ingredients when they realised the recipe called for twelve eggs.
sentences.putting: She was ____________________ the finishing touches on the display when the headteacher walked in.
sentences.dropping: The temperature was ____________________ rapidly as the sun disappeared behind the ridge.
sentences.skipping: The pupil admitted to ____________________ the difficult questions and coming back to them at the end.
sentences.hitting: The hail was ____________________ the greenhouse roof so hard that nobody could hold a conversation.

starter.question: Can you add -ing to these verbs? What must you do first?
starter.ruleBox: Short vowel + single consonant before -ing: double the final consonant (sit→sitting, run→running). Long vowel or consonant cluster: just add -ing (help→helping, sleep→sleeping).

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Look at each base verb. Why does the final consonant double?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words double the final consonant before -ing. The rule: short vowel + single consonant = double before a suffix (sit→sitting, run→running). If the vowel is long or ends in a cluster, no doubling is needed. This keeps the short vowel sound safe — without doubling, 'siting' would suggest a long vowel as in 'kite'.

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: Possibly from be- (around, thoroughly) + ginnan (to open or start).

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Used throughout Middle English as biginnen; the spelling settled to begin by the 1400s.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use beginning to mean the point at which something starts.

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: The final n in begin is short and single, so it doubles before -ing: begin → beginning.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box1label: No doubling — long vowel or cluster
wordSort.hint: Say the base verb. Is the vowel short (sit) or long (sleep)? Does it end in a cluster (help, jump)?
wordSort.answerNote: No doubling: helping, reading, jumping, starting, sleeping. Double: sitting, running, swimming, shopping, hitting.
wordSort.exampleLine: help → helping (cluster, no double) | sit → sitting (short vowel + single consonant, double)

wordShed.def: the point at which something starts
wordShed.sentence: The beginning of the novel was so gripping that the librarian had to remind her the library was closing.
wordShed.morphology: begin (v) → beginning (pres part / n) → began (past simple) → begun (past part) → beginner (n) → beginners (n pl)
